correctness.rationale: The source norm and operator identity reduce the problem to the weighted supremum of the canonical basis function. The source bound |phi_n(z)|<=epsilon_n^{-1}|z|^n is attained for positive real z because the defining Pochhammer convolution equals (2lambda+1)_n/n!=epsilon_n^{-2}. Hence the norm is exactly (n+lambda+1)epsilon_n^{-1} max_r (1-r^2)r^n. Elementary differentiation gives r^2=n/(n+2), and the gamma-ratio asymptotic gives the stated leading constant. No finite experiment is used to infer an infinite or exact statement.

value.rationale: The phi_n form the canonical H_lambda^2 orthonormal basis and are basic building blocks of the new lambda-Bloch theory. Their exact norm is therefore a natural invariant of the newly introduced space. The result separates a universal extremal radial scale 1-r_n~1/n from the reflection-dependent amplitude n^lambda and supplies an exact leading constant useful for future basis, coefficient, and embedding estimates.
